scope: sampled visual and story review; ASR and measured signal support; no validated audio listening
product_from_film: GRU Space presents a machine intended to make building material from lunar regolith as a step toward off-world habitation.
explains_well: Dark machine close-ups and marked material samples make the engineering ambition tangible.
unclear: The film does not clearly separate the current prototype, its test conditions and the future lunar hotel imagery.
scenario: Develop a machine intended to manufacture bricks from lunar material.
product_clear_basis: Text says the machinery will use lunar regolith to manufacture bricks on the Moon.

scenes.action: Text says lunar regolith will be used to manufacture bricks on the Moon. Close-ups show material in a small container, rotating or changed machine positions, round openings and a shaped piece near the tool.

scenes.purpose: Show a physical manufacturing process, with exact stages and continuous operation unclear from the samples.

scenes.action: A card claims the patent-pending Moon Factory was designed, built and tested in six weeks. Material samples include an American flag pattern and a GRU imprint. Another card describes enabling life on the Moon, Mars and beyond.

scenes.purpose: Present a development milestone and a tangible branded output.
scenes.evidence: Visible chronological 1 fps samples, source 77–92s; boundary approximate; exact motion between samples unverified.

scenes.action: Text says the first payload could land on the Moon as early as next year. A Moon image gives way to a pixel-edged GRU roundel against stars.
scenes.design: Sparse white type, lunar image and logo.
scenes.purpose: End with a future milestone rather than a user action.
scenes.evidence: Visible chronological 1 fps samples, source 92–98.345s; boundary approximate; exact motion between samples unverified.

lessons.keep: Use a real-looking physical output to make a broad mission concrete, while stating its evidence limits.
lessons.avoid: Avoid blending future concept imagery and present prototype evidence without labels.
lessons.open: Material and test conditions, machine continuity, hotel imagery status, launch timing and all heard audio remain unverified.
try: For Tin, label the working prototype and show one complete workflow before the future roadmap.
Place a measurable result beside the final artifact so its meaning is clear without a long founder explanation.
